items.stem: Removing a sensitive attribute like race from the data will:

options.text: Not necessarily remove bias, because correlated proxy variables can remain
options.rationale: Correct: proxies can reintroduce the same bias.
Proxy variables mean bias can persist.

options.text: Make the model illegal to use
options.rationale: Removal does not determine legality by itself.
Fairness definitions can still be violated.

items.explanation: Correct: proxies can reintroduce the same bias.

items.stem: Which TWO reflect sound data-ethics practice? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Collect only the data necessary for the stated purpose
options.rationale: Correct: data minimisation reduces risk and respects people.

options.text: Keep a human accountable for consequential automated decisions
options.rationale: Correct: accountability cannot be delegated to 'the algorithm'.

options.text: Assume anything legal is automatically ethical
options.rationale: Legal and ethical obligations are not identical.

options.text: Collect maximum data in case it is useful later
options.rationale: Over-collection violates minimisation and increases risk.

items.explanation: Correct: data minimisation reduces risk and respects people.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: An automated system makes a harmful decision. Which stance is ethically sound?

options.text: A named human or body remains accountable and must provide redress
options.rationale: Correct: accountability stays with people, not the tool.

options.text: No one is accountable because the algorithm decided
options.rationale: 'The algorithm decided' does not remove human accountability.

options.text: The affected person bears all responsibility
options.rationale: Shifting blame to the affected person is not ethical.

options.text: Accountability is unnecessary if the model is accurate
options.rationale: Accuracy does not remove the need for accountability.

items.explanation: Correct: accountability stays with people, not the tool.
